headline: CAM, Khaitan, SAM, Latham act on Shiprocket ₹1,617 crore IPO
sum: Shiprocket, India's largest new-age end-to-end e-commerce enablement platform, raised ₹1,617.48 crore through a book-built IPO comprising ₹885.50 crore fresh issue and ₹731.98 crore offer for sale, listing with 35% premium on 19 August 2026. The issue was oversubscribed 102.28 times with strong institutional participation (QIB at 122.80x, NII at 88.99x, retail at 46.42x), debuting at ₹131 on NSE (35.05% premium to ₹97 issue price).
implication: Shiprocket as a professionally-managed, no-identifiable-promoter VC-backed platform demonstrates the market's appetite for tech-enabled logistics enablers; the dual-counsel model (issuer counsel CAM/SAM, selling shareholders counsel Khaitan, BRLMs counsel SAM/Latham) illustrates standardised governance for complex multi-stakeholder tech IPOs with material OFS components.
detail: The Shiprocket IPO was structured as a 100% book-built issue of 16,67,61,566 equity shares (face value ₹10) priced at ₹92–₹97 per share. The fresh issue (9.13 crore shares, ₹885.50 crore) was earmarked for platform growth, technology infrastructure (₹211 crore), marketing (₹294–306 crore), and debt repayment (~₹210 crore). The OFS (7.55 crore shares, ₹731.98 crore) involved 16 selling shareholders including early-stage VCs (500 Startups, Tribe Capital, LR India Fund, Agility), quasi-promoters (Eternal/Zomato, Bertelsmann, Arvind), and co-founders. Bidding opened 12 Aug, closed 14 Aug 2026; allotment 17 Aug; listing 19 Aug on NSE (designated) and BSE. Company raised ₹727.42 crore from anchor investors pre-IPO. The issue was subscribed 102.28x overall, with retail garnering 48.38x, QIBs 125.20x, and NIIs 92.58x. Shares debuted at ₹131 on NSE and ₹129.50 on BSE. The company, incorporated in 2011 (initially as Bigfoot Retail Solutions) and now registered in New Delhi with HQ in Gurugram, has no identifiable promoter under SEBI ICDR Regulations, reflecting professional VC-backed governance. FY26 financials: revenue ₹2,024 crore (+24% CAGR FY24–26), adjusted loss ₹76 crore (vs ₹351 crore in FY24), positive operating cash flow.

structure.novel: Primary novel feature: professionally-managed, no-identifiable-promoter entity (VC-backed, multi-tier cap table across 128 shareholders pre-IPO) navigating SEBI ICDR Regulations without traditional promoter disclosure. Secondary novelty: significant dual-counsel structure where issuer counsel and OFS counsel operate separately (CAM/SAM for issuer and co-founder sellers; Khaitan for institutional sellers); BRLMs counsel (SAM and Latham & Watkins) advised on regulatory and structuring matters with cross-border investor participation (Luxembourg SAIF, US LPs, Singapore-based Temasek, India-based quasi-promoters).
